newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Kohl arrives to sign Czech-German declaration.
newsitem.headline: Kohl arrives to sign Czech-German declaration.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl arrived in the Czech Republic on Tuesday to sign a Czech-German declaration intended to set the seal on post-World War Two reconciliation between the two neighbours.
Kohl, on his first visit to an independent Czech Republic, was greeted at Prague airport by Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, with whom he was scheduled to sign the declaration later on Tuesday.

In the accord, Bonn expresses its sorrow for the Nazi occupation of Czech territory between 1938 and 1945 and Prague its regret at Czech brutality in the post-war expulsion of some 2.5 million Sudeten Germans.
The declaration, reached after two years of talks, also includes German support for Czech membership of the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
The Czech Republic, the last of Germany's neighbours not to have signed a post-war reconciliation pact, is a leading contender to be among the first new members of both groups.

However, the accord is controversial in both countries. Czech communists and far-right Republicans planned protest demonstrations to coincide with Kohl's visit. The German leader is due to leave Prague on Wednesday.
